Theme

School & learning

fiction noun

also fictional, fictitious, made-up, made up, a work of fiction, fact and fiction, stranger than fiction

classical

Cic. Lael. 97: in rēbus fictīs et adumbrātīs (Lewis & Short, s.v. fingō)
Cic. Lael. 24: in rē fictā, opposed to in vērā (Lewis & Short)

rēs fictae, rērum fictārum f. pl.

fiction, things made up

The participle of fingere, “to make up”: what is invented, as against rēs vērae. As an adjective, fictus is “fictional, made up”, of a story as of anything else (Cic. Off. 3.39), and alone ficta are inventions (Cic. Off. 2.43). For a story as such, see story.

Other words

  • fābula, fābulae f. — a story, a tale; fiction, myth

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Liv. praef. 6 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Any story told (see story), and so a tale that is not history: Livy sets the poets’ tales against unspoilt records of what was done. In the plural, as a kind of writing, it does for “fiction”.

  • commentum, commentī n. — invention, fabrication

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.5: opīniōnum commenta dēlet diēs (Lewis & Short); Ter. And. 1.3.20 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    From comminīscī, to think up: an invention, usually one passed off as true, so “a fiction” in the sense of a lie.

  • fābulōsa narrātiō — fiction (as a kind of writing)

    also used · modern · Traupman 314

    fābulōsus is classical, “legendary, fabulous” (Hor., Suet.; Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • incidī in māteriam vēram sed simillimam fictae

    I’ve come upon a story that is true but very like fictionPlin. Ep. 9.33.1

  • calumniārī sī quis autem voluerit, quod arborēs loquantur, nōn tantum ferae, fictīs jocārī nōs meminerit fābulīs

    and if anyone wants to carp because trees talk, not only beasts, let him remember that we are playing in made-up talesPhaedr. 1 prol. 5–7

  • opīniōnum commenta dēlet diēs

    time wipes out the inventions of opinionCic. N.D. 2.5 (Lewis & Short)

See also story, plot, imagine, tell a story.
